newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES ADVANCE 0.65PCT ON UPBEAT BLUE CHIPS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES ADVANCE 0.65PCT ON UPBEAT BLUE CHIPS.

text.p: Greek equities climbed for the third consecutive session, led by increased interest in blue chip banks, industrials and OTE telecom.
"Prices are moving higher helped by growing demand and a fairly flat supply of stock in blue chips," said Dimitris Kontoes, broker at ABN AMRO-Axias Securities.
"The only spot where supply outstripped demand was Alpha Credit Bank and Ergobank against a background of hot buying into state banks like National and Natl Mortgage," he added.
Construction met with profit-taking following a two-day aggressive advance.

"Construction ran into profit-taking after a substantial rise in two days which was based on renewed optimism about Athens' bid for the 2004 Olympics rather than a change in fundamentals," said Kontoes.
Athens along with Rome are the favourites to host the games. The selection will take place September 5. Other candidates are Buenos Aires, Stockholm and Cape Town.

The Athens benchmark index added 0.65 percent or 10.56 points to 1,639.44, which was the day's high, from Thursday's 1,628.88, helped by late buying which accounted for around half of the day's gains.
Banks were upbeat but weakness in Alpha Credit and Ergobank limited overall gains to 0.15 percent.
Industrials were up 0.91 percent but construction shed 1.23 percent.
Turnover rose slightly to 13.4 billion drachmas on volume of 3.7 million shares.
Advancers beat decliners 101 to 99 with 37 shares unchanged on 237 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.6-$11.0. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,124-1,154 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,094-1,154 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock firmed 170 drachmas to 6,445.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 685.12-728.85 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $74.92-$77.73. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,850-4,079 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.08 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 251-283 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
